TEXT.English: [BOLD]Strategy:[\BOLD][PARAGRAPH:1]The Apache Confederacy is built for elastic warfare: strike quickly, avoid losing momentum, and keep pressure on the border until your opponent breaks. Your core package rewards fighting in difficult terrain and sustaining conflict over time rather than relying on a single decisive stack battle. Apache cities can turn into reliable troop engines early, and your mobile units remain threatening well beyond their normal timing window.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][BOLD]Background:[\BOLD][PARAGRAPH:1]The Apache peoples formed a network of related communities across the American Southwest and northern Mexico, adapted to harsh climates, long distances, and constant strategic movement. Their military traditions emphasized mobility, scouting, surprise, and survival under pressure. In game terms, this civilization represents a unified Apache state that combines those traditions into a cohesive frontier empire. It favors commanders who can manage tempo, punish overextension, and repeatedly convert small tactical advantages into lasting territorial control.[PARAGRAPH:1]When played well, the Apache Confederacy should feel resilient rather than explosive: a civilization that wins by outmaneuvering stronger economies, preserving veteran units, and forcing wars to be fought on Apache terms.

TEXT.English: [H1]Geronimo[\H1][NEWLINE][BOLD]Leader of the Apache Confederacy[\BOLD][PARAGRAPH:2][BOLD]Background:[\BOLD][NEWLINE][TAB]Geronimo is remembered as one of the most determined resistance leaders of the Apache world, associated with endurance, mobility, and the refusal to yield under sustained pressure. His legend was not built on static empire management, but on surviving repeated campaigns, preserving fighting strength, and forcing stronger enemies into costly pursuits across difficult country.[PARAGRAPH:1]This design interprets Geronimo as a commander of tempo and attrition. He is strongest when wars are active and frequent, when border fighting creates repeated opportunities for Great General generation, and when veteran mounted or gunpowder forces can keep initiative turn after turn. Rather than chasing a single crushing offensive, Geronimo rewards disciplined pressure: raid, disengage, reinforce, and strike again before the opponent can stabilize.[PARAGRAPH:1]In practical terms, Geronimo players should think like field commanders: maintain a core of promoted mobile units, use terrain to control engagements, and turn every favorable skirmish into long-term strategic advantage.

TEXT.English: The Apache Raider replaces the Horse Archer as a stronger and more evasive skirmisher. It hits harder than the base unit and remains effective in hilly ground where mounted warfare usually slows down.

TEXT.English: Use Apache Raiders to harass workers, isolate siege, and repeatedly pressure border cities. Their high withdrawal chance and hill combat bonuses make them excellent for sustained raids instead of one decisive charge.

TEXT.English: The War Council replaces the Barracks and turns each military city into a steadier recruitment center. In addition to core barracks training, it improves morale and speeds wartime mobilization.

TEXT.English: War Councils grant +2 unit experience, +1 happiness, and +15% military unit production. Prioritize them in your main production line to compound veteran output over long wars.
